g.text: - UserID
- AuthToken
- Cancel()
- Timeout()
User
get all trucks
GET /trucks
get logged in user
Auth Service
Truck Service
GET /routes
get truck routes
Route Service
Example when User is making the API call.
Track API is going to for each track or for a batch
of tacks will get the routes of truck is going to.
Middleware is Auth Service - when user login and send
GET /truck the middleware Auth will check if the
user is actually logged in or not, if is we're going to inject the user metadata
into the context. We will have a handler that will have user data like
User ID, his first Name, E-mail, all of that - only possible using context
(middleware - context).
* The same context may be passed to functions running in different goroutines,
contexts are safe for simultaneous use by multiple goroutines.
! Important for us because the handlers on an HTTP server are usually a goroutine.
Another example is when user making calls to GET trucks and this calls the server Route
and the server Route is maybe down so user will wait some time for response.
To user not to wait and check for response quite some time, we will use a Timeout()
which will set for operation some time to exec(6s) and if there is not response
we will canceled. With go is very easy to use.
! Context - is has a box that carries contextual information about request. So the power of context is to
carry information and ability to control the flow around the functions.
Initializing context: context.Background() or context.TODO()
! Context is immutable - cannot change or modify same.
